title: Convex Hull
statementMd:
You are given $n$ quadratic inequalities, each of the form

$$ a_i x^2 + b_i x + c_i \gt 0 $$

It is guaranteed that $a_i \lt 0$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.

Determine whether there is an **integer** $x$ satisfying all $n$ inequalities simultaneously.z

## Input

The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 10^4$), the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer $n$ ($1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5$), the number of inequalities.

Each of the next $n$ lines contains three integers $a_i,b_i,c_i$ ($-10^5 \le a_i \le -1$, $-10^5 \le b_i,c_i \le 10^5$), the coefficients of the $i$-th inequality.

The sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \times 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output `YES` if such an integer $x$ exists, or `NO` otherwise.

The answer is case-insensitive; for example, `yes`, `YES`, `Yes`, and `YeS` are all accepted as affirmative answers.

## Note

Sample 1 Explanation

In the fourth test case, $x=0$ satisfies both inequalities, so an integer solution exists.
